facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: For three thousand years thou shalt wander over this earth, without a companion and without being able to talk with anyone.
facts.text: Krishna curses Ashwatthama to roam the wilderness devoid of human companionship and suffering from disease for three thousand years.

facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: Drona's son, then, having made over his gem to the high-souled Pandavas, cheerlessly proceeded, before their eyes, to the forest.
facts.text: Ashwatthama surrendered the divine jewel embedded in his forehead to the Pandavas before departing into exile.

facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: Always engaged in sinful acts, thou art the slayer of children. For this reason, thou must have to bear the fruit of these thy sins.
facts.text: The divine curse was cast on Ashwatthama as retribution for directing the Brahmashira weapon against the womb of the pregnant Uttara.

facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: Those excellent words that Devaki's son has said, will, without doubt, be realised in thy case.
facts.text: The sage Vyasa affirmed Krishna's decree that Ashwatthama would live solitary in the forest stinking of blood and pus.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: The whole fort , including all the walls, Sat Darwaza, the mosque and temple inside. Asirgarh. Burhanpur.
facts.text: The entire complex of Asirgarh Fort, including its ramparts and gateways, is cataloged as a protected monument of national importance by the Archaeological Survey of India.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: Mahadeo Temple with its compound near the inspection Bunglow. Asirgarh. Burhanpur.
facts.text: The Archaeological Survey of India separately protects the medieval Mahadeo temple and its precinct situated near the inspection bungalow within Asirgarh.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: The chronology begins in 1978 with the theft of a Shivlinga from the ASI-protected Asirgarh Fort in Burhanpur.
facts.text: Official heritage crime documentation recorded the unrecovered theft of a stone Shivalinga from Asirgarh Fort in the year 1978.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: Popularly known as the 'dakkhan ka darwaza' or gateway to the Deccan, Asirgarh Fort situated in the outskirts of Burhanpur gained importance for its location.
facts.text: Asirgarh Fort stands in the Satpura Range roughly 20 kilometers north of Burhanpur, historically commanding the primary pass connecting northern India to the Deccan plateau.

facts.label: disputed
facts.quote: In the Mahabharata, Ashwatthama is cursed to wander the earth for three thousand years, not forever.
facts.text: Textual scholars note a contradiction between the critical edition of the Mahabharata, which bounds Ashwatthama's curse to 3,000 years, and widespread folklore that asserts he must endure till the end of the Kali Yuga.

facts.label: disputed
facts.quote: Constructed in the early 15th century by King Asa Ahir, this fortress, known as the 'Key to Deccan,' played a pivotal role in controlling southern India.
facts.text: Historians dispute the origins of Asirgarh Fort, with Persian chronicler Ferishta attributing its foundation to the 15th-century chieftain Asa Ahir while other accounts suggest earlier medieval Hindu occupation.

facts.label: legend
facts.quote: It is said that Krishna cursed Ashwatthama with immorality & no moksha thus, he still wanders in Asirgarh Fort and offers prayer & flowers to Lord Shiva.
facts.text: Local folklore at Asirgarh claims that freshly plucked red flowers and sandalwood paste appear each morning on the Shivalinga of the Gupteshwar Mahadev temple before opening.

facts.label: legend
facts.quote: One of them was a doctor from Madhya Pradesh who, some years ago, had said that a patient with an unusual wound on his forehead came to him to get it treated.
facts.text: A popular urban legend recounts that a modern physician in Madhya Pradesh treated an exceptionally tall patient bearing a deep, unhealing forehead cavity.

facts.label: legend
facts.quote: Jokingly he once asked the patient if he was Ashwatthama. He said that after saying this, as soon as he turned to look at his patient, the latter had vanished from his cabin.
facts.text: According to the doctor sighting legend, the wounded patient vanished without a trace the moment the practitioner jokingly asked if he was Ashwatthama.

facts.label: legend
facts.quote: A strange man roaming around the Narmada river seeking oil to soothe on his forehead, he was described as a tall person.
facts.text: Folklore in the Nimar forests along the Narmada and Tapti river belts claims a towering nomad occasionally asks ascetics and travelers for mustard oil and turmeric to soothe an aching brow.
